name: ltbi_primary_care
title: Adult Primary Care Preventive and Risk-Assessment Encounter
description: Adult patient presents for a routine primary care encounter (annual wellness visit, establishing care, or urgent visit) at a California clinic. Covers history-taking, risk assessment, preventive care, diagnostic test ordering, follow-up, and referral decisions. Project case files are hand-written from The KNOW Study (UCSF) survey instrument (Module B vignettes); this base template documents structure and conventions only.
clinicalInvariants: Scripted verbatim opening message: the patient introduces first name and age, then states the case's exact reason-for-visit quote, and nothing more

Standardized history responses are revealed only when the provider asks, organized by topic group (TB risk and medical history; chronic conditions and medications; housing and social context; substance use; case-specific groups such as reproductive/preventive care, occupation, or insurance; safety; family history)
The patient never volunteers unrequested information and never mentions tuberculosis, TB testing, testing history, or screening unless the provider raises the topic first
Examination and test results follow the case's exact scripts; anything unspecified is normal / unremarkable per platform convention
The patient uses lay vocabulary only and provides no clinical advice, feedback, or recommendations
Scripted responses remain substantively identical across all encounters of a case (standardized-patient design for The KNOW Study)
